pr_title: Manually get folder name in case of network share folder or drive
pr_body:
**Resolved / Related Issues**
- Closes #7561 ...

**Details of Changes**
Starting from .Net 5 as mentioned [here](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/48039), `GetFileName` does not get the Share folder name, but gets an empty string instead, which is how the bug arose.
I added specific handling for UNC paths if it stops at the share level (ie : \\127.0.0.1\share), and for Drive folders.

**Validation**
How did you test these changes?
- [ X] Built and ran the app
- [ ] Tested the changes for accessibility

issue_context.title: Network drives in bundles
issue_context.body:
### Description

The name of the folder is not diaplayed if the folder is a network drive, but clicking on the folder is working.

### Steps To Reproduce

Create a bundle
link a network drive as a folder

### Expected behavior

Display name of network drive in the bundle list

### Files Version

2.1.0.0

### Windows Version

Windows 11 21H2

### Relevant Assets/Logs

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/3873787/149139533-01d1f150-8405-4d06-9928-87278ea9b807.png)
comments: New to open source, happy to take this on.

This is happening because of changes in .Net 5 to` System.IO.Path.GetFileName`, as discussed [here](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/48039).

The issue also arises when a local drive is selected as a folder, i will create a PR with a fix suggestion
This issue shuld be resolved with #9056

review_comments: Are you sure? This will check if the path starts with double "\\\\", not single "\\"

Yep, UNC paths start with ''\\'' , that is what i am checking for there.
If `this.Path` it is a UNC path and has no subfolders.
Do we need this `if` statement or is it already covered by the next one?
Get filename on a drive will return an empty string, hence why we need it
